definition: Lexical choice is the subtask of Natural language generation that involves choosing the content words (nouns, non-auxiliary verbs, adjectives, and adverbs) in a generated text.
details: Function words (determiners, for example) are usually chosen during realisation.
story: Think of a jazz musician who has heard so many solos that a new one simply falls out of their fingers. Here is the short version: Lexical choice is the subtask of Natural language generation that involves choosing the content words (nouns, non-auxiliary verbs, adjectives, and adverbs) in a generated text. The part that makes it sing: Function words (determiners, for example) are usually chosen during realisation. Creation, here, is memory recombined at speed. And that is Lexical choice — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
